Flood risk (satellite-only)

Risk: Low Grade: C

Annual probability 0.0% (roughly once every 4,171,447 years); credible range 0.0% – 6.4%.

How this estimate was reached

  1. Satellite-only mode: no hydrometric gauge or HYDAT record was used; every quantity below is observable from space + terrain.
  2. Terrain: HAND computed on the 30 m national DEM (MRDEM), channel scale 5.0 km2; this address sits 4.9 m above the nearest mapped channel.
  3. Flood history: 38 years of optical water observations (JRC Global Surface Water, 1984-2021) were binned by HAND to give an empirical wet-probability curve for THIS reach; monotonicity in height is enforced (water cannot prefer higher ground).
  4. The curve evaluated at the address's HAND gives the central annual probability 0.0%; the credible range 0.0%-6.4% combines within-band spread, spatial-correlation-deflated sample size, and the Bayesian posterior.
  5. Observed flood extents: none available for this window yet — the estimate rests on the occurrence history alone.
  6. Model constants: satellite-only defaults (occ_to_annual=1.0, px_decorr=25.0, prior_w=8, channel_km2=5.0)
  7. Regional flood history (40 km window): the 38-year JRC occurrence record is a frequency, not a dated-event list; per-event flood history awaits the EGS extent connector (M-SAT-1).

Regional context

Mandatory caveats

  • No in-situ gauge: the evidence grade is capped at C by construction. A gauged HazardWise report supersedes this one wherever it exists.
  • Optical occurrence under-counts short-duration and under-cloud floods, so the central probability is best read as a LOWER bound of that evidence channel; the upper credible bound carries that asymmetry.
  • SAR/optical water mapping is unreliable under dense canopy and in built-up cores; occurrence there reads low regardless of true flooding.
  • The occurrence-to-annual-probability mapping is an interim disclosed form (constant above); it is replaced, not tuned.

Wildfire risk (archive-only)

Risk: Low Grade: C

Annual probability 0.0% (roughly once every 13,341 years); credible range 0.0% – 0.0%.

How this estimate was reached

  1. Wildfire, satellite/archive-only mode: no in-situ fire-weather station or provincial assessment was used.
  2. NBAC loaded: 0 perimeter-years in window, 53-yr record.
  3. Burn history: 0 NBAC perimeter-years over a 53-year record; the mean annual fraction of burnable land burned in this window is 0.0165% (CI 0.0000%-6.7584%) — the regional base rate.
  4. Local exposure: this address is 0 m from continuous wildland fuel (exposure e-fold 500 m) on 2 deg terrain (slope multiplier up to 1+0.5).
  5. Annual burn probability = 1 - exp(-rate x exposure x slope), updated per-pixel by observed burned-year counts (Beta-Binomial; pixel trials deflated 5x for correlation with the regional rate, which the same years estimated).
  6. The graded number is REACH probability: the maximum within 250 m of the address (0.01%, vs 0.01% at the exact pixel) — a fire at the fence line is the risk to the structure.
  7. Reach-back: no mapped historical burn intersects this window.
  8. Result: 0.01% central (CI 0.00%-0.02%) -> Low.
  9. Regional-rate floor applied: the 40 km burn history implies a base rate of 0.0165%, above the 0.0000% measured inside the 3 km map window; the higher, region-supported rate is used so this number cannot contradict the history below (B2).
  10. Model constants: fire defaults v0.22 (wui_decay=500.0 m, slope_boost=0.5, c=1.0, prior_w=8)
  11. Regional fire history (40 km window): Past 10 years: 5 mapped fires (NBAC >=200 ha) (years: 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2018); nearest 6.3 km (2025). Past 20 years: 10 mapped fires (NBAC >=200 ha) (years: 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2018, 2012, ...); nearest 4.4 km (2009). Past 50 years: 22 mapped fires (NBAC >=200 ha) (years: 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2018, 2012, ...); nearest 4.4 km (2009).

Regional context

Mandatory caveats

  • Archive-only: grade capped at C. NBAC maps burns >~ 200 ha reliably; small/urban-interface fires are under-represented, so the central value is a lower bound of this evidence channel.
  • No fire-weather forecast is included: this is climatological frequency, not current-season danger (CWFIS FWI is the M-FIRE-2 addition).
  • The exposure/slope form is an interim disclosed model; it is replaced, not tuned (Lever 3).
